newsitem.title: USA: Co-ops oppose Texas electric deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Co-ops oppose Texas electric deregulation bill.

text.p: Local electric co-operatives over the weekend withheld support for legislation that would open the Texas electric grid to competition, lobbyists and analysts said on Monday.

That support was considered critical to getting the bill voted out of Texas' House State Affairs committee, and lengthened the odds a deregulation bill would be passed in Texas in the final weeks of the biennial legislative session, they said.
"We think its chances are pretty slim," HSBC James Capel analyst Nahla Azmy said.

The compromise House proposal would open markets to competition on January 1, 2002, cut residential rates by 10 percent, freeze commercial rates and allow utilities to recover stranded costs by depreciation and securitization.

In a hearing late Friday, the co-ops came out against the lengthy bill in part because of uncertainty over dense language spelling out how utilities would recover stranded costs as the grid was opened to competition, lobbyists said.

The state's investor-owned utilities were expected this week to mount an intense lobbying campaign to either garner support from the co-ops or gather enough votes to move the bill out of committee despite the co-ops' opposition.
"We have heard that the utilities are going to try to jam this through without the support of the co-ops," one lobbyist representing independent power marketers said.

Lobbyists said the bill must be voted out of committee this week to meet deadlines for scheduling a vote on the House floor and referring the measure to the Senate if it passes. The timing of those votes was uncertain, and the bill could die in committee if no vote is called by the committee chair.
